keyframe_review.note: 7,101 km2 in Texandria (the southern Netherlands and northern Belgium), 358-438. The page has the Salians in Texandria, 'relatively unpopulated and infertile', after Constans let Franks settle there 'already in 342 AD, after fighting there in 341 AD', and has Julian's terms 'authoriz[ing] the Salians to keep any lands they had settled without fighting' (c. 358). The page gives no boundary and no area (no infobox), so the infobox comparison is not possible. The outline stands to 444 (see 439).

correction.text: the Frankish realm after Soissons: the Salian land with the Domain of Soissons, its border on the Loire

keyframe_review.note: 166,379 km2: the Salian realm and Syagrius's Domain of Soissons 'between the Somme and the Loire' (Cliopatria's 490 shape contains 524 of the 525 cells of its Kingdom of Soissons shape of 480-489). The page: 'Consequently, the realm of the Franks almost doubled in size; its border was now on the Loire.' Cliopatria's shape is four times the 452 shape (41,165 to 166,379 km2); 'almost doubled' fits only if the page's baseline is all Frankish land, Ripuarian Franks included (44,276 + 41,165 = 85,441 km2; ratio 1.95), which is a reading. The Clovis I page has the Roman kingdom 'probably under Clovis's control by 491', Cliopatria starts 490; the page gives no year for the completion. The Kingdom of Soissons page (reread after the review) gives no boundaries and says scholars divide between 'a state controlling most of northern Gaul' (the maximalist view) and Edward James's 'Count of Soissons' who 'controlled a small area'; Cliopatria's Soissons shape (about 125,000 km2 added to the Salian 41,165) is the maximalist reading and is larger than the doubling the battle page states. That page dates Syagrius's death '486 or 487' (MacGeorge 485/486, Martindale 486/487).

Unchanged outline for 490-495 (it starts four years earlier in keyframe 486); for 496-499 take keyframe 496. One doubt left as drawn: the shape holds about 10,900 km2 of eastern Brittany, while the Clovis I page has Clovis lead his troops to Armorica only 'in 501, 502 or 503'; the Soissons page says 'between the Somme and the Loire' and does not say whether the Domain reached Brittany. Unverified within the page budget. The Kingdom of Soissons page (reread after the review) is silent on Brittany and Armorica (neither term appears), so the 10,900 km2 stay unverified.

region.text: Texandria, south of the Rhine-Meuse delta, the lands the Salians had settled without fighting

ledger.note: 358: Julian lets the Salian Franks keep Texandria. The page dates Julian's conflict with the Salians 'around 358 AD', a Salian deputation at Tongeren in the 'winter of 357/8 AD', and has his terms 'authoriz[ing] the Salians to keep any lands they had settled without fighting', with the Salians supplying soldiers to Rome. Texandria is named, not bounded; Constans had let Franks settle there 'already in 342 AD'.

region.text: Tournai, Cambrai and the country up to the Somme, in Belgica Secunda

ledger.note: 445: Chlodio takes Tournai and Cambrai. 'The Frankish conquest of Turnacum and Cameracum probably happened in the period 445-450' (Lanting & van der Plicht 2010); Chlodio 'occupied the country up to the Somme' (Gregory), 'in the heart of Belgica Secunda'. The page gives a span; 445 is its first year. Cliopatria draws the shape from 439.

region.text: the Domain of Soissons between the Somme and the Loire

ledger.note: 486: Clovis wins at Soissons and takes Syagrius's domain. 'The Battle of Soissons was fought in 486' between the Franks and 'the Gallo-Roman domain of Soissons under Syagrius', who 'preserved his father's rump state, the Domain of Soissons, between the Somme and the Loire'; 'its border was now on the Loire'. The page does not date the completion of the conquest; the Clovis I page has the kingdom 'probably under Clovis's control by 491' and Cliopatria's shape grows in 490.

minus.text: the southern half of the Alamannic lands, south of about 48.5 N (Switzerland and Rhaetia), which 'sought protection under Theoderic'

region.text: the northern half of the Alammanian lands

ledger.note: 496: Clovis beats the Alamanni at Tolbiac. 'As a result of Clovis' victory, the northern half of the Alammanian lands went to the Franks while the southern half sought protection under Theoderic' (the Tolbiac page, reread; 'The date of the battle has traditionally been given as 496', a revised chronology gives 506; the Clovis I page: 'in the Battle of Tolbiac in 496'). Repaired after review: the region used to be Cliopatria's whole Alamannia shape (475 cells, about 120,000 km2), contradicting its own text. It is now that shape minus a polygon south of about 48.5 N, which removes 224 cells (about 56,650 km2, Switzerland and the Lake Constance country) and leaves 251 cells (about 63,500 km2: Alsace north of Strasbourg, the Palatinate, Lorraine, the Moselle with Trier). The page gives the extent as a half, not a line: the 48.5 N cut is my reading of 'half' (the cell count halves there), and the Alamannia page (reread) gives no 496 line either, only the later duchy's borders (Murg-Heilbronn-Nördlinger Ries in the north, the Lech, the lower Aare). Cliopatria hands its whole Alamannia shape to the Salian row in 500.

region.text: Armorica (Brittany) beyond the land already in the Salian shape

ledger.note: 501: Clovis leads his troops to Armorica. 'In 501, 502 or 503, Clovis led his troops to Armorica.' 'Armorica and its fighters were thus integrated into the Frankish realm.' Brittany west of what Cliopatria's Salian shape already holds is added; the counterpart is Cliopatria's Brythons row, which holds western Brittany (the page's people are the 'Armorici').

507: Clovis wins at Vouillé and takes most of Aquitaine. 'Armorici assisted him in defeating the Visigothic kingdom of Toulouse in the Battle of Vouillé in 507'; 'The battle added most of Aquitaine to Clovis's kingdom.'
508: Clovis makes Paris his capital. 'The election of Paris as capital must have also happened around 508' (the Salian Franks page: Clovis 'established his capital in Paris').

wars.name: Julian's campaign against the Salian Franks
wars.outcome: The Salians sent a deputation to Tongeren in the winter of 357/8; Julian authorised them to keep the lands they had settled and they had to supply soldiers to the Roman army.
wars.note: The page dates the conflict 'around 358 AD'; the Franks page (opened for ripuarian-franks) has 'In the spring of 358 the Salian Franks were described under that name for the only time in written history'.

wars.name: Chlodio's conquest of Tournai and Cambrai

zones.text: Tournai, Cambrai and the country up to the Somme

wars.outcome: The Franks hold Turnacum and Cameracum and the country up to the Somme.
wars.note: Dated 'probably ... 445-450' by Lanting & van der Plicht (2010); the page has no reign dates for Chlodio and no year for a defeat at Vicus Helena.

wars.name: Childeric I's Loire campaigns
wars.outcome: Childeric fights near the Loire and takes Angers after Count Paul's death; no dated change of border.
wars.note: Gregory's Loire fighting is 'generally equated to the Battle of Orléans (463)', which scholars question; Angers is undated; the Gothic revolt of Euric is 'around 469'. The Saxons at Angers are led by Adovacrius.

wars.name: Battle of Soissons

zones.text: the Domain of Soissons between the Somme and the Loire

wars.outcome: Clovis defeats Syagrius, who flees to the Visigoths and is handed over for execution; the Domain of Soissons ends and the Frankish border reaches the Loire.
wars.note: Chararic 'stood aloof, hoping to ally with the winner'. A single decisive battle: the page gives no campaign span, so no contest span is recorded.

wars.name: Clovis's campaign against the Thuringians
wars.outcome: 'Clovis allegedly moved against a small number of Thuringians in eastern Gaul, near the Burgundian border'; no territory recorded.

wars.name: Battle of Tolbiac

minus.text: the southern half of the Alamannic lands, south of about 48.5 N (Switzerland and Rhaetia), which 'sought protection under Theoderic'

zones.text: the northern half of the Alammanian lands

wars.outcome: The Alamanni are defeated and their leader killed; the northern half of their lands passes to the Franks.
wars.note: Traditional date 496; a revised chronology (Van de Vyver, from Theodoric's letter of 506/7) gives 506. Zone repaired after review: the northern half of Alamannia only.

wars.name: Clovis's war against Gundobad at Dijon
wars.outcome: 'After some months, Clovis was convinced to abandon the siege and settled for an annual tribute from Gundobad.' No territory changes hands.
wars.note: The page does not say how long the tribute lasted, so no vassal event is written. The Gundobad page (reread after the review) says Aridius 'convinced him to spare Gundobad in return for a yearly tribute', dates the Clovis-Gundobad-Godegisel fighting to 500 (Marius of Avenches) and Godegisel's murder to 501, and gives no end for the tribute.

wars.name: Clovis's Armorican campaign
wars.outcome: 'Armorica and its fighters were thus integrated into the Frankish realm.'

wars.name: Battle of Vouillé
wars.outcome: The Visigothic kingdom of Toulouse is defeated; 'The battle added most of Aquitaine to Clovis's kingdom.'
wars.note: Armorici assisted Clovis (Clovis I page); Sigobert of the Ripuarian Franks supported him 'in the spring of 507' (Sigebert the Lame page, opened for ripuarian-franks).

certainty.note: No treaty line anywhere in the life: Julian's 358 terms name Texandria but no boundary, the Somme and the Loire are rivers named by the Soissons page, and the Alemannic, Armorican and Aquitanian lands are approximate. Every frontier is soft.

notes:
Salian Franks (eu-07-a). Pages: five of the five-page budget (Salian Franks, Clovis I, Battle of Soissons (486), Childeric I, Chlodio) plus two pages opened under the ripuarian-franks budget and reused for the Alemannic gain (Tolbiac) and the 509 merger (Ripuarian Franks). The Salian Franks page has no infobox, no capital and no area; none of the pages gives an area, so no infobox comparison was possible (the Soissons page says only that the realm 'almost doubled in size').

Cliopatria rows. (1) The Salian 490 shape is the 452 shape plus the Kingdom of Soissons shape (524 of 525 cells), and the 500 shape is the 490 shape plus the Kingdom of Alamannia shape (474 of 475 cells): the gains in this ledger therefore name kingdom-of-soissons and kingdom-of-alamannia. Cliopatria's Alamannia shape (3.66-11.06 E, 47.0-50.44 N) reaches Lorraine and holds Trier from 462; the Tolbiac page says only 'the northern half'. For eu-06 to compare. (2) Cliopatria's Kingdom of the Franks row 462-509 (28,600 km2, 4.15-7.15 E, 48.9-51.5 N, holding Cologne from 462) is disjoint from the Salian and Ripuarian shapes (zero common cells in 470 and 505); for the owner of kingdom-of-the-franks to decide whether it is the Cologne core of the Ripuarian kingdom or a third Frankish state. (3) The kingdom-of-soissons and visigothic-kingdom dossiers name kingdom-of-the-franks as receiver of the 486 and 507 gains; Cliopatria's shapes put Soissons in the Salian row and Aquitaine in no Frankish row. Clovis's realm is one state in the pages (Salian kingdom to 509, Franks after); Phase C should reconcile the counterpart slugs.

Dates settled by reading. 445 (span 445-450), 486 (battle) against 490 (Cliopatria, and 'by 491'), 496 (traditional; 506 revised) against 500, 501 (the page allows 501-503). Brittany: Cliopatria's Salian shape holds about 10,900 km2 of eastern Brittany from 486 (left as drawn, page silent) and none of the west; the Clovis I page integrates 'Armorica' in 501-503; the Breton groups (kingdom-of-brittany, breton-kingdoms) write the later story.

Not written, and why. No contest events: the pages give single battles (Soissons, Tolbiac, Vouillé) with no campaign span. No vassal event for Gundobad's tribute (500/501): the page does not say when it ended. No rulers strip: the pages date only Childeric (c. 457/458-481) and Clovis (481-509); earlier kings (Chlodio, Merovech) have no dates there. No capital before 445. Childeric's Loire fighting (463-469) and the Saxon defeat at Angers are undated or disputed on the page and moved no Cliopatria border. Month: none of the pages gives one.

Gazetteer names wanted: Texandria/Toxandria (region), Tournai and Cambrai (places), Zülpich (place, the Tolbiac site), Tongeren (place). Counterpart needing a dossier: Ragnachar's Frankish kingdom of Cambrai (the Franks page: Clovis 'later defeated Ragnachar, king of Cambrai'; Clovis I: murders of Sigobert and Ragnachar, 509), not in Cliopatria.


Repairs after the review (2026-10-19). (1) The Tolbiac gain was Cliopatria's whole Kingdom of Alamannia shape (about 120,000 km2) although the page, reread, says 'the northern half of the Alammanian lands went to the Franks while the southern half sought protection under Theoderic': ledger 496, keyframes 496, 500, 501 and 507, the Tolbiac war zone, ledger 509 and identity.successors[0].land now subtract a polygon south of about 48.5 N (224 of the shape's 475 cells, about 56,650 km2; the cut is my reading of 'half', the page and the Alamannia page draw no line), and keyframe 500 is adjust for the land as well as the years. The earlier statement that the page is silent on the extent was wrong. (2) The 509 gain from the Ripuarian kingdom and the 509 dissolve add Cologne (and Trier, as in ripuarian-franks), which the Cliopatria Ripuarian 509 shape lacks. (3) War 0 starts in 358 (applied by the reviewer). (4) Keyframe 486 now says in its note that Cliopatria's Soissons shape is the maximalist reading and larger than the page's doubling. Thin checks: the Kingdom of Soissons page is silent on Brittany (10,900 km2 stay unverified); the Gundobad page gives no end for the tribute (no vassal event). The Aetius page (opened for the Ripuarian thin check) has 'Aetius then defeated the Franks, recapturing Tournacum and Cambriacum' in 431 and Chlodio's attack on Atrebatum in the 440s, which sits uneasily with the 445-450 conquest of Tournai and Cambrai taken from the Chlodio page: the dossier keeps the Chlodio page's dating and Phase C may weigh the two. Sources are now 11 against a budget of 5: four pages were added for the repairs and thin checks.
